new_in_run21.plateau_gate_bump_first: Two code changes landed + test-proven: (1) coverage_plateau_exhaust default 2->1, so a SINGLE no-new-coverage frontier batch exhausts the movement frontier and hands off to bump/interaction discovery (runs 17-20 pegged the whole 80-action budget on frontier re-sweeps and never reached a 2-batch plateau). (2) BUMP-FIRST ordering: new _frontier_fully_covered(frame, frontier) infers the frontier batch's predicted player cells (cells that differ across predicted_grids, level-keyed, same inference as _update_coverage) and, when coverage was RESUMED (coverage_resumed_pct>0) and EVERY predicted cell is already in _coverage_cells, trips the plateau immediately BEFORE running the redundant batch -- so a resumed run re-treading known ground goes straight to bump probing. Conservative: fires only on resumed coverage; a fresh run legitimately sweeps its first batch. Tests: plateau=1 hands off to bumps within a tight toy budget; _frontier_fully_covered true iff batch is pure resumed re-sweep; bump-first trips plateau with resumed coverage without a redundant frontier batch. Full ewm suite (349) + --smoke green.

why_bumps_did_not_fire_live: Plateau=1 landed and is test-proven, but the live run STILL fired 0 bumps -- for the two compounding reasons this run isolated. (1) The frontier NEVER PLATEAUS within 80 actions even at threshold 1: frontier_batches=11, coverage_pct=0.05 (identical shape to runs 18-20). Each ~16-action open-loop batch endpoint lands on at least one FRESH cell, so the coverage-plateau counter RESETS every single batch and never reaches even 1-in-a-row-with-no-new-ground before the budget is exhausted. Lowering the threshold 2->1 is necessary but INSUFFICIENT: the batch granularity is coarse enough that every batch opens new ground. (2) The BUMP-FIRST resumed-coverage shortcut could not engage because coverage was never RESUMED: coverage_resumed_pct=0.0. Root cause -- the coverage-persistence WRITE failed (POST /overlay/note timed out / 404, KB note write failed for 'game ls20 coverage chunk 1 of 1'), because the bounced daemon re-saturated to 100% CPU under its drain backlog and note WRITES block behind the graph mutation lock the drains hold. So coverage_persisted=false -> next run has nothing to resume -> the bump-first gate (guarded on coverage_resumed_pct>0) can never fire live until the persistence write path is unblocked. Next levers: (a) plateau on PREDICTED coverage or make _frontier_fully_covered fire on a FRESH sweep too (not only resumed) so a batch whose PREDICTED endpoint re-treads known ground hands off without waiting for the empirical plateau; and/or (b) raise the action budget well past 80 so the movement frontier genuinely plateaus; and (c) a daemon whose WRITE path is not starved by drains, so coverage actually persists and resumes across runs.
